proposed_widenings.name: UseCountCap { kind: 'unlimited' }
proposed_widenings.justification: The ring has no per-activation limit — it can be activated any number of times. ActivatedAbilityMechanics requires an ActivationResource whose cap must be one of: fixed, threshold_tiers, linear_per_level, proficiency_bonus, ability_modifier. None expresses 'unlimited.' Encoding with fixed:1 or any concrete cap would misrepresent the rule.
proposed_widenings.evidence: While wearing this ring, you can take a Magic action to give yourself the Invisible condition.

proposed_widenings.name: permanent duration endsOn: 'wearer_bonus_action' (or DurationEndTrigger { kind: 'wearer_spends_bonus_action' })
proposed_widenings.justification: The invisibility ends when the wearer voluntarily spends a Bonus Action to dismiss it. The v4 lifecycle atom 'self_break' covers this concept, but the surface does not expose it. The permanent duration's endsOn only accepts 'dispel' | 'damage'; DurationEndTrigger covers externally-caused ends (attack roll, damage taken, etc.) but not a deliberate wearer-initiated dismissal. A new variant is needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You remain Invisible until the ring is removed or until you take a Bonus Action to become visible again.

notes: The ring fits the magic_item / activation family structurally, and the effect atom (apply_condition invisible on self via direct phase) encodes cleanly. Both blockers are surface-level variants of existing types: (1) UseCountCap needs an 'unlimited' variant for items with no activation cap; (2) the duration end mechanism ('wearer spends Bonus Action') maps to the v4 self_break lifecycle atom but is not reachable from any current Duration field. The 'until ring removed' end condition is arguably implicit in the item/attunement lifecycle and may not need a separate surface variant.
